articles.name: Announcing AMB invitation messages
articles.title: Announcing AMB invitation messages
articles.body:
Starting November 23, 2026, businesses using Apple Messages for Business can proactively start conversations with customers by sending a branded, verified invitation message directly to the customer's mobile number.

This article includes the following sections:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Apple Messages for Business conversations could previously begin only when the customer messaged the business first. With Invitation Messages, an authorized business can now reach out proactively. The invitation appears natively in the customer's Messages app with the business's verified name and logo. When the customer taps Yes and replies, a standard two-way Apple Messages for Business conversation begins in Zendesk.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

These branded and verified invitations appear natively in the Messages app on Apple devices, allowing customers to easily engage with businesses in secured and private conversations. Because the invitation is delivered by Apple itself, the business's identity is verified end to end.

What do I need to do?

If you already have an Apple Messages for Business channel with Zendesk, the feature is available through the Sunshine Conversations Clients API.  No Zendesk-side setup is required. You must complete this step before sending invitations:

  • Request enablement from Apple. Email messagesforbusiness-support@apple.com with your Business ID and Business Name. Apple reviews the request and enables Invitation Messages for your business manually. Invitations fail until this is done.

To send an invitation, create a link request through the Create Client endpoint of the Sunshine Conversations API, targeting the customer's phone number in tel: format and including your brand name and logo (PNG, 200 kB or smaller; a square image is recommended). See the Create Client API documentation for the full request schema.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Service Incident - October 28, 2026 -  Forethought AI Agents  |  Pod 20  - Dashboard authentication outage
articles.title: Service Incident - October 28, 2026 -  Forethought AI Agents  |  Pod 20  - Dashboard authentication outage
articles.body:
Summary

On October 28, 2026, from 15:10 UTC to 16:54 UTC, some Forethought AI Agents customers on Pod 20 were unable to sign in to their dashboards. Affected users received the message, “PreAuthentication failed with error There was an error retrieving user information.” No data loss was observed.

 

Timeline

October 29, 2026 17:38 UTC | October 29, 2026 10:38 PT

On October 28th, 2026 between 15:10 and 16:54 UTC some customers were unable to access their Forethought dashboards. An error message, "PreAuthentication failed with error There was an error retrieving user information" was presented when some agents attempted to log in. We do not observe any lasting impact after 2026-10-28 16:54 UTC when corrective action was taken, nor do we expect any reoccurrence for this issue. A post mortem will be shared in Service Notifications once we have completed our internal root cause analysis. Thank you for your understanding and our apologies for the inconvenience this caused as well as our delayed notification of this incident.

 

Root Cause Analysis


This incident was caused by a missing readiness configuration in the service supporting Forethought Dashboard sign-in. During a deployment, existing servers were shut down before the load balancer registered their replacements as healthy. As a result, sign-in requests were directed to servers that were no longer available, preventing some customers from accessing their dashboards.

Resolution

A subsequent deployment refreshed the load-balancer targets, restoring dashboard sign-in. We then added a readiness configuration to coordinate server replacement with load-balancer target health. Testing showed that this change prevented the load balancer from losing all healthy targets during deployments.

Remediation Items

  • Updated the deployment configuration to help keep dashboard sign-in available while servers are being replaced.
  • Tested the updated configuration to confirm that healthy servers remain available during deployments.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

articles.name: Announcing procedure improvement recommendations for copilot auto assist
articles.title: Announcing procedure improvement recommendations for copilot auto assist
articles.body:
Zendesk is introducing procedure improvement recommendations to help you refine your published procedures for auto assist. These recommendations make iterating and improving procedures simpler.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

A new recommendation called "Update procedure" is now available. Admin copilot analyzes procedures after your publish them and may recommend changes to:

  • Reflect how agents work with auto assist suggestions generated based on procedures
  • Clarify the structure of procedures
  • Improve the formatting of procedures

For example, you may see suggestions to:

  • Update procedure steps if agents handle a task differently from steps in a procedure.
  • Clarify the structure of a procedure if it's confusing for auto assist to follow.
  • Format a procedure differently if its structure is not optimized.

What do I need to do?

Review your recommendations periodically. When a procedure has recommendations, it's marked by a violet sparkle. Open the procedure to review the suggestions inline in the editor and accept or dismiss them. 

To learn more, see Reviewing knowledge recommendations.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing the update organization action in action flows
articles.title: Announcing the update organization action in action flows
articles.body:
We're happy to announce that you can now use the update organization action in action flows to automatically update organization records as part of your automated workflows.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Previously, updating organization records required manual intervention or external API calls. Now, you can add the update organization action directly into your action flows.

The action supports both standard organization fields and custom fields. When configuring custom drop-down fields, the available values appear directly in the action interface so you can easily select the exact value to apply.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

To help you streamline customer management, we are expanding action flows to support native organization updates. By automating organization field changes, your teams can keep account statuses, tiers, and metadata accurate in real time without manual data entry.

What do I need to do?

You don't need to do anything. This feature is automatically rolled out to all eligible accounts.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

Summary

On November 13, 2026, from approximately 18:21 UTC to 18:42 UTC, a subset of Zendesk Support customers on Pods 13 and 19 received HTTP 429 errors and “Access temporarily restricted” notifications while updating tickets.

 

Timeline

November 13, 2026 19:21 UTC | November 13, 2026 11:21 PT

We are investigating reports of 429 errors and growler notifications stating “Access temporarily restricted. You’ve reached your activity limit. Try again later.” Our engineers are looking to identify the root cause and mitigate any impact. If possible, please capture a HAR file to aid in our investigation.

November 13, 2026 20:04 UTC | November 13, 2026 12:04 PT

We have recovered from the spike of traffic that temporarily caused some customers to receive 429 errors and growler notifications stating “Access temporarily restricted. You’ve reached your activity limit. Try again later.” We are monitoring to ensure stability, and we will provide another update when we have reached full resolution.

November 13, 2026 20:11 UTC | November 13, 2026 12:11 PT

We are happy to report that we have resolved the issue causing a subset of customers to receive 429 errors and growler notifications stating “Access temporarily restricted. You’ve reached your activity limit. Try again later.” Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a planned traffic-routing change that increased traffic to a new routing layer faster than sufficient capacity became available. The resulting traffic exceeded the layer’s per-instance rate limit, causing some requests to receive HTTP 429 responses.

 

Resolution

The service automatically added capacity in response to the increased traffic, after which error rates returned to normal. We monitored the service to confirm stability and subsequently completed the remaining traffic transition using additional capacity without recurrence.

 

Remediation Items

  1. Updated the traffic-transition procedure to add and verify sufficient capacity before increasing traffic.
  2. Improved retry handling for temporary rate-limit responses.

  3. Validated the revised procedure during the subsequent traffic transition.

articles.name: My AI agent triggers two use cases for a single message
articles.title: My AI agent triggers two use cases for a single message
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

A customer sends a single message that contains more than one request. For example: "I want to cancel my subscription, and can I get a refund?"

Your AI agent then performs the following actions:

  • Identifies more than one intent in the message
  • Triggers two use cases, such as a use case for the request and a Knowledge reply
  • Sends two separate responses instead of one combined response

This can make the resolution confusing for the customer.

How can I resolve this?

Root cause

This is expected behavior for multi-intent conversations in messaging.

When the AI agent identifies multiple intents in a conversation, it performs the following steps:

  1. Evaluates the identified intents and triggers the corresponding use cases or flows configured for those intents
  2. Identifies and runs the appropriate use case for each intent independently
  3. Updates the customer during or after each use case, depending on how that use case is configured

Each use case can have different steps that the AI agent must complete on its own. The AI agent may therefore not be able to give one summary that covers the whole conversation.

Resolution steps

You can't turn off multi-intent handling. The following options may make the responses more consistent.

Option 1: Add an instruction to combine responses

  1. Create a new instruction to guide how the AI agent summarizes responses across compatible topics when it detects multiple intents. For example: 'If the customer's message includes more than one request, summarize the responses into a single reply when the topics are compatible.'
  2. Apply the instruction
  3. Test your AI agent with a message that contains both intents
Note: AI agents are non-deterministic, which means they may not respond the same way every time. Instructions influence the AI agent's responses, but they can't guarantee the same behavior in every conversation. Test the instruction with several messages and adjust the wording as needed.

Option 2: Review use cases that only perform a Knowledge search

  1. Review the use cases involved in the duplicate responses
  2. If a use case only performs a Knowledge search and has no other actions or steps, consider removing it. For example, this might apply to a "Subscription Cancellation Request" use case that only searches your knowledge base.
  3. The Knowledge Reply use case can then handle those requests. This may give more consistent summaries, including in conversations where the AI agent identifies multiple intents.
  4. Test your AI agent again
Note: Only remove a use case if it has no other actions or work items. Results may vary.

Summary

Delayed inbound processing could also cause ticket comments to appear out of order.

Timeline

We’re continuing to coordinate with Microsoft on the issue affecting inbound and outbound mail delivery through the Zendesk Microsoft Exchange Connector. Microsoft is still working to resolve the issue on their end. We’re monitoring progress and will share another update when we have more information.

November 13, 2026, 06:30 UTC | 10:30 PM PST:

Inbound and outbound mail delivery through the Zendesk Microsoft Exchange Connector continues to be disrupted. Microsoft has also declared an incident and is working to restore service. November 13, 2026, 15:02 UTC | 7:02 AM PST:

Microsoft have reported significant progress on this issue, and we can tell we are also gradually recovering based on the observed error rate. We are preparing to re-send outbound mail that was queued during this incident. Inbound mail has been continuously automatically retried, and we are monitoring the success rate of mail ticket creation. Due to the inbound mail delays, this may result in ticket comments appearing out of order.

November 13, 2026, 17:24 UTC | 9:24 AM PST:

We are still monitoring recovery and keeping a close watch at Microsoft’s progress towards full resolution of this incident. We are progressing on our own recovery and are still backfilling delayed outbound mail. We will provide an update when this is complete.

We are happy to report that we have completed our backfill and have fully recovered from the issue affecting incoming and outbound email delivery using the Microsoft Exchange Connector. Thank you for your patience as we worked to resolve this issue and restore functionality.

 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a Microsoft service disruption in which the process used to establish secure connections became overwhelmed, causing affected Microsoft servers to stop responding. This prevented the Zendesk Microsoft Exchange Connector from reliably processing inbound and outbound email, resulting in delayed or failed email delivery for customers using the connector.

Resolution

To fix this issue, Microsoft restored the affected services, allowing the Zendesk Microsoft Exchange Connector to resume processing email. Inbound email was automatically retried, and we reprocessed failed outbound email, completed the backfill, and performed delivery spot checks to confirm recovery.

Remediation Items

  1. Update the email recovery script to process delayed outbound email in parallel, reducing recovery time.
  2. Create a runbook documenting how to identify and recover failed email delivery.
  3. Improve failed-email notifications so customers can identify delivery failures and take recovery action.

articles.name: Workflow: Setting up AI agent responses to typed text instead of button selections
articles.title: Workflow: Setting up AI agent responses to typed text instead of button selections
articles.body:
Use a conditional branch in the AI agent flow to detect when an end user enters free-form text instead of selecting one of the presented button responses. Track those attempts with a custom parameter such as free_text_selected, then route the conversation based on how many attempts have occurred.

Use this workflow when your AI agent presents predefined button choices, but you want to limit how many times an end user can type a custom response before the AI agent redirects or escalates the conversation.

The workflow includes the steps below.

Step 1: Verify the prerequisites

Before you update the flow, verify that the required setup is in place:

  • An AI agent flow with a step that presents button options
  • A custom parameter to track free-text attempts, such as free_text_selected
  • A fallback path, such as escalation to an agent or transfer to another branch

After you confirm these prerequisites, update the dialogue to handle typed responses more effectively.

Step 2: Update the AI agent use case dialogue

Update the AI agent use case dialogue to detect when an end user types a response instead of selecting a button option, and route the conversation using a conditional block.

  1. Open the AI agent flow you want to update
  2. Go to the step where the AI agent presents button responses
  3. Create or confirm a custom parameter named free_text_selected
  4. Add an action after the button response step for the Fallback outcome to update your free_text_selected parameter, then add a Conditional block below it to evaluate the parameter
  5. Configure the condition to evaluate the free_text_selected parameter
  6. Set the threshold for the number of free-text attempts you want to allow. For example, use Less than or equal to 3 to allow three typed responses before escalation.
  7. In the branch where the value is within the limit, add an AI agent message block to prompt the customer again to choose one of the available buttons
  8. In the branch where the value exceeds the limit, send the conversation to your Fallback outcome, such as escalating to an agent, transferring to another workflow branch, or providing alternate instructions and ending the conversation
  9. The completed flow looks like this:
  10. Save and test the flow to confirm the branch behaves as expected

After you save your changes, the dialogue re-prompts the end user or routes the conversation to a fallback path based on the configured attempt limit.

Step 3: Test the AI agent

Test the updated flow to ensure that the AI agent handles typed responses as expected and triggers the correct branch at the right point.

After you complete testing, confirm that the flow follows the intended retry and escalation behavior. For more information, see Testing conversation flows in AI agents.

articles.name: Why do I receive the error "language was not recognized" in AI agents?
articles.title: Why do I receive the error "language was not recognized" in AI agents?
articles.body:
Question

In some cases, I see the error language was not recognized in AI agents. Why does this happen and how can I fix this?

Answer

You receive this error when the AI agent can't set a language for the conversation. The AI agent stores the conversation language in the active_language session parameter. If this parameter is empty or incorrect, the AI agent can't reply in the customer's language.

The AI agent sets active_language in one of three ways:

  • The content of the customer's first message
  • An integration with your CRM, such as Sunshine Conversations, or a Conversation started action
  • The customer's language selection in the welcome message, if you configured one

Language detection runs when active_language is empty. This happens on the first message, if the AI agent didn't save the language, or if you reset the language. After the AI agent sets active_language, new messages don't override it. The value only changes if an action changes it.

For more information, see Detecting the customer’s language.

Note: Language detection works best on messages longer than five words. The AI agent might not detect the language of a message that has only one or two words.

To fix this error, check how your account populated the active_language value, if at all. Review the conversation logs for an affected conversation to see which value the AI agent set. For more information, see Reviewing conversation logs for AI agents.

Then check each source in the list below:

  1. Check the customer's first message. Did the message contain more than five words? A short first message, such as "Hola" or "Help", can prevent a correct detection. Review your conversation logs to see which first messages customers typically send.
  2. Check your CRM integration and actions. Look for any action on the Conversation started event that sets active_language, such as a Sunshine Conversations action. Verify that the action saves the value as active_language. Verify that the locale ID matches the locale ID of a language you added to the AI agent. Locale IDs are case sensitive and require an exact match, for example en-US. Verify that the CRM field the action retrieves contains a value for this customer.
  3. Check the welcome message. If your welcome message asks customers to select a language, verify that each button sets a language that you added and activated for the AI agent.
  4. Check for actions that set the language manually. If an action sets active_language, the AI agent keeps that language. It replies in that language even if the customer later writes in a different one. Update the action or add an action that changes the language when needed.

After you correct the source, start a new test conversation to confirm that the AI agent replies in the expected language.

articles.name: Why is the WhatsApp composer missing in Agent Workspace?
articles.title: Why is the WhatsApp composer missing in Agent Workspace?
articles.body:
Question

Why doesn't the WhatsApp composer appear in Agent Workspace on a WhatsApp messaging ticket, and why can only some agents see options such as Internal note or other non-WhatsApp channels?

Answer

A common reason is that the agent doesn't have the required Chat access or Chat role to participate in messaging conversations.

In Agent Workspace, the WhatsApp messaging composer appears only when an agent has permission to work messaging conversations. If an agent doesn't have active Chat access, the WhatsApp composer doesn't appear on the ticket. As a result:

  • WhatsApp may not appear as a selectable reply channel
  • The template selection experience doesn't appear
  • The agent may see only options such as Internal note or other non-messaging reply options

This behavior can be confusing because the WhatsApp channel may appear missing, but agent access causes the issue rather than a template-sync or ticket-channel problem.

When this applies

This explanation is relevant when all or most of the following are true:

  • The ticket is a WhatsApp or messaging ticket
  • Admin Center displays approved or active WhatsApp templates
  • The customer expects template sending to remain available outside the 24-hour session window
  • Some agents can see the WhatsApp composer, but other agents can't
  • The affected agent can make public comments, but WhatsApp still isn't available in the composer

Why templates are also missing

WhatsApp templates depend on the WhatsApp composer experience. If the composer doesn't appear for the agent, the template option is also unavailable.

Expected product behavior

If an agent lacks the required Chat access, the product may omit the WhatsApp composer entirely rather than showing WhatsApp in a deactivated state. In that case, the absence of the WhatsApp option is expected behavior for that agent.

Example symptom pattern

  • Agent A does not have Chat access → WhatsApp composer is missing
  • Agent B does have Chat access → WhatsApp composer and template option are visible

How to verify and resolve

Identify the agents who must reply to WhatsApp conversations, and confirm that those agents have the required Chat role or access.

To check whether the affected agent has the required messaging-related access:

  1. Open the agent's profile or settings in Admin Center
  2. Confirm that the agent has the appropriate Chat Agent role
  3. Confirm that the agent has active Chat access
  4. Test the same WhatsApp ticket using an agent who has Chat access
  5. If WhatsApp appears for the agent with Chat access but not for the affected agent, this strongly indicates an agent-access issue rather than a WhatsApp template availability issue

Additional resources

  • Giving agents access to messaging channels
  • Getting started with social messaging
  • Understanding default roles for live chat and messaging
  • About conversational support with messaging

articles.name: Using video calling with screen sharing in Contact Center
articles.title: Using video calling with screen sharing in Contact Center
articles.body:
Video calling lets you see a customer and share screens while keeping the conversation connected to a ticket. You can start a video call from the channel switcher or move an active voice call to video.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

Use video calling to see your customer and share screens while keeping the conversation connected to a ticket. Start a call from the channel switcher or move an active voice call to video. You and the customer can control audio and video, share screens, and access tickets during the call; audio may be recorded and transcribed, but video and shared screens aren’t.

Video calling lets you see a customer and share screens while keeping the conversation connected to a ticket. You can start a video call from the channel switcher or move an active voice call to video.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Preparing for a video call
  • Starting a video call
  • Using video call controls
  • Ending a video call

Preparing for a video call

You must have access to the call console and video calling in Contact Center to start a video call. If the video option isn't available, ask your admin to give you access.

Check your browser has permission to use your camera and microphone. Your customers, or end users, also need to allow access if they want you to see and hear them.

Video calls support one agent and one customer. You can't transfer or schedule a video call, or start screen sharing without a video call. Audio can be recorded and transcribed, but video and shared screens aren't recorded.

Note: Screen sharing is limited on mobile devices. When screen sharing is not supported you won't be able to share the screen because the share button is disabled.

Starting a video call

You can start a video call from the channel switcher or from an active voice call. When moving from voice to video, stay on the voice call while the customer joins. The voice call ends automatically when the video call is accepted.

To start a video call

  1. From the channel switcher or active voice call, select Video.

  2. Click Generate code.

    It expires after three minutes. If it expires, generate and share a new code.

  3. Share the video URL and code with your customer.

    You can tell them the URL and code during a voice call or send it in a message using an available channel.

    The URL is the same for video calls across tickets in your account.

  4. (Optional) Guide the customer through joining the call.

    Share Joining a Contact Center video call as an end user.

  5. Wait for the customer to join the call.

    You can only join the call when you receive a notification after the customer has selected their devices and clicked to join the call.

  6. Click the microphone icon to mute or unmute your microphone and the camera icon to start or stop your video.

    You can also click Manage call preferences, to select audio and video devices other than your system defaults. Once you start the call you cannot pick other devices but you can control the microphone and camera.

    If your admin has configured you to automatically accept calls, you might have little to no time to select different devices other than your defaults.
  7. If calls aren't automatically accepted, click Accept, or click Switch to video if you're on an existing voice call.

    If automatic acceptance is configured, the video call is accepted automatically. You join the customer on the video call.

Using video call controls

During a video call, you and the customer can mute or unmute your microphones, turn your cameras on or off, and share your screens. You can also minimize the video call to access your Agent Workspace. The call controls appear in the call bar at the bottom of the screen.

You and the customer can share your screens at the same time.

To access your workspace and tickets

  • Click the minimize icon.

To mute or unmute your microphone

  • Click the microphone icon.

To turn your camera on or off

  • Click the camera icon.

To share your screen

  1. Click the screen share icon.
  2. If a permissions dialog opens, allow screen sharing.
  3. Select the tab, window, or screen to share.

  4. Click Share.

    When you or the customer share a tab, the address bar is hidden.

  5. Click the screen share icon again to stop sharing.

Ending a video call

Either participant can end the video call. When the call ends, you enter wrap-up.

To end a video call

  1. In the call bar, click the end call icon ().
  2. In the End call? dialog, click End call.

    The call audio recording and transcript, if available, are added to the ticket.

  3. Complete any required ticket fields and add notes to the ticket.
  4. Click Finish wrap-up to conclude your work.

    If your agent settings have an after call work timeout, you can let that time run out to conclude the work. For more information about wrap-up, see Ending a call.

Article Q&A

Click to view

What do I need to use video calling, and what are its limitations?

You need access to the call console and video calling in Contact Center, and your browser must have permission to use your camera and microphone. The customer must allow camera and microphone access if you want to see and hear them. Calls support one agent and one customer; you can't transfer or schedule them, or start screen sharing without a video call. Audio may be recorded and transcribed, but video and shared screens aren't recorded. Customer screen sharing may be unavailable on some mobile devices.

How do I start a video call and invite my customer?

Select Video from the channel switcher or an active voice call, then click Generate code and share the video URL and code with the customer by voice or message. The code expires after three minutes, so generate and share a new one if needed. The URL is the same across video calls in your account. You can share the end-user joining instructions, then wait for a notification that the customer has selected devices and joined.

How do I move an active voice call to video and choose my devices?

Stay on the voice call while the customer joins. Before starting the video call, use Manage call preferences to select audio and video devices other than your system defaults, if needed. Click Accept or Switch to video to join; the voice call ends automatically when the video call is accepted. Once the call starts, you can control your microphone and camera but can't select different devices. If calls are automatically accepted for you, you may have little or no time to choose devices.

How do I share my screen or access my tickets during a video call?

Use the call bar at the bottom of the screen. Click the minimize icon to access your Agent Workspace and tickets. To share your screen, click the screen share icon, allow screen sharing if prompted, select a tab, window, or screen, and click Share. You and the customer can share screens at the same time. When a tab is shared, its address bar is hidden.

How do I end a video call and finish my work?

Click the end call icon in the call bar, then click End call in the confirmation dialog. Either participant can end the call. You'll enter wrap-up, and the call audio recording and transcript, if available, are added to the ticket. Complete required ticket fields, add notes, and click Finish wrap-up. If your agent settings include an after-call work timeout, you can let it expire to conclude your work.

articles.name: Troubleshooting Gmail fallback
articles.title: Troubleshooting Gmail fallback
articles.body:
In this article, you'll learn how to troubleshoot the Gmail fallback when Gmail can't send an outgoing ticket notification. Fallback is an attempt to send the message through Zendesk's email infrastructure, not a guarantee of delivery, so this article also covers what to check if a recipient still doesn't receive the email.

The guide includes the topics below.

Troubleshooting Gmail fallback

Check whether the Gmail connection is active. If it has disconnected, follow the steps in Managing Gmail connections. If you see an invalid OAuth credentials error or cannot find Reconnect, see I can't reconnect my support address through the Gmail connector in Zendesk Support.

Review the About Google sending limits section. If you use a domain your organization owns, check whether its SPF record authorizes Zendesk to send.

For an address at a domain your organization owns, GC-901 can appear if the domain’s SPF record is invalid or does not authorize Zendesk to send email. In that case, fallback is not attempted. Ask your domain administrator to review Allowing Zendesk to send email on behalf of your email domain for SPF setup. If Admin Center also shows an SPF, DNS, or TXT record error, see Troubleshooting email error messages on forwarding, SPF, DNS, and TXT records for error-specific steps.

If Gmail cannot send a notification while fallback is off, or if a fallback attempt fails, agents see a delivery error on the affected ticket. In Agent Workspace, check below the ticket comment in the conversation log or open the ticket events log. If a warning icon appears next to a recipient, select it for details. Review the error and the recipient address or receiving-server policy as appropriate.

Even when fallback is attempted, the recipient’s mail server may reject the message or place it in spam. Ask the recipient to check their spam folder or contact their email administrator. For more recipient-side checks, see Troubleshooting email deliverability under “Verify delivery status with the recipient.”

To test that incoming email creates tickets and a public reply reaches your test address, see Testing your email setup. This checks general email delivery; it does not confirm that fallback was used.

Check email status with the API

Admins can check the current email delivery status for each recipient of a known ticket with the Email Notifications API. If Zendesk mail servers try to send a fallback message and it fails, the status may show an SMTP code instead of a Gmail Connector code. That code describes the mail-server delivery attempt, not the original Gmail problem.

Fallback does not guarantee delivery, and a later status may replace the fallback-attempt status.

articles.name: What options do I have to review when agents sign in or out?
articles.title: What options do I have to review when agents sign in or out?
articles.body:
Question

What options do I have to review when agents sign in or out of Zendesk Support?

Answer

There are a few options depending on your plan and add-ons that can help track agent session and activity data.

Option 1: Audit Log (Suite and Support Enterprise plans)

The audit log captures agent sign-in timestamps. While it does not record sign-out times, it can help you confirm when an agent last signed in.

To view agent sign-in activity in the audit log:

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Logs > Audit log
  2. Set the Activity type filter to Signed in
  3. Under Item > Type, select Team member
  4. Optionally, use the Names field to filter results for a specific agent

For more information, see How can I check agent sign-in timestamps?

Option 2: Access Log (Advanced Data Privacy and Protection add-on required)

The access log records agent activity such as tickets viewed, user profiles accessed, and searches performed within the last 90 days. While it does not log explicit sign-out events, it can help identify when an agent last had activity in the account.

To view the access log:

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Logs > Access log
  2. Use the Actor field to filter by a specific agent's name or email address
  3. Use the Start date and End date filters to narrow the time range

For more information, see Using the access log to monitor agent activity.

Option 3: workforce management (WFM add-on)

If your account has the workforce management add-on, the Agent Attendance page provides more detailed session and attendance reporting, which may better meet your needs for tracking agent activity over time.

For more information, see About the Agent attendance page.

Option 4: Omnichannel agent state dataset in Analytics

You can also use the Omnichannel - Agent state dataset or Omnichannel - Agent state daily dataset in Analytics, formerly Explore, to report on agent states.

This dataset provides timestamped event information, including when agents enter and leave states such as Online and Offline. You can use these state start and end times to report on agent availability.

Analytics results may not accurately reflect an agent's sign-out time if the agent closes the browser or leaves the workspace without explicitly signing out. In that case, the agent may continue to appear as online for that period. For the most accurate reporting, remind agents to manually sign out at the end of their shifts.

For more information, see Explore recipe: Reporting on agent state.

articles.name: Configuring spam and junk email filtering
articles.title: Configuring spam and junk email filtering
articles.body:
Zendesk uses spam filters to identify incoming email that may be spam, junk, or otherwise risky. Admins can configure how Zendesk handles each type of identified email. This gives you more control over the balance between blocking unwanted email and allowing legitimate email that may have characteristics commonly associated with spam.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Configure spam and junk email filtering to control whether incoming emails are accepted as tickets or sent to the suspended tickets queue. Choose default, accept, or suspend for categories such as phishing, scams, spam, bulk marketing, and low-reputation senders. When an email matches multiple categories, the strictest setting applies; malware is always suspended.

Zendesk uses spam filters to identify incoming email that may be spam, junk, or otherwise risky. Admins can configure how Zendesk handles each type of identified email. This gives you more control over the balance between blocking unwanted email and allowing legitimate email that may have characteristics commonly associated with spam.

This article contains the following topics:

  • About spam and junk email filtering in Zendesk
  • Understanding your configuration options
  • Configure spam and junk email filtering

Related articles:

  • What does "Detected as spam" mean?
  • Understanding and managing suspended tickets and spam

About spam and junk email filtering in Zendesk

Zendesk uses spam filters to assess whether an incoming email looks suspicious. The filters consider a range of signals related to the message, its sender, and the email’s delivery or authentication setup. Zendesk doesn’t publish the specific algorithms or exact rules used, and no single characteristic necessarily means a message will be flagged. Depending on the assessment, a message may be placed in the Suspended tickets view for review.

Zendesk identifies potential spam and junk email using the following categories. An email can be assigned to more than one category.

Category Description
Phishing Email that may attempt to obtain sensitive information or direct recipients to unsafe websites.
Scam or fraud Email that may be associated with deceptive or fraudulent activity.
Strong spam signals Email with strong indicators that it is likely spam.
Weak spam signals Email with less conclusive indicators that it may be spam.
Marketing and bulk email Promotional messages, newsletters, and other bulk-sent email.
Low reputation senders Email from senders that have indicators of a low or potentially risky reputation.
Adult content Email containing or promoting adult-oriented content.

Understanding your configuration options

Initially, your account uses the Zendesk spam filter's default settings. For each spam category, you can override the default setting and choose to always create a ticket for emails in that category or suspend those emails.

The following are your options for tickets in each category:

  • Default: Use the Zendesk default filtering behavior for the category.
  • Accept: Create a ticket for emails in this category.
  • Suspend: Email in the category is sent to the suspended tickets queue.

When an email matches multiple categories, Zendesk applies the strictest outcome. For example, if an email matches two categories and either category is set to Suspend, Zendesk suspends the email.

Protections that always apply

Some email protections are always in place, and aren't affected by your spam filtering settings:

  • Email containing malware or viruses is always suspended.
  • Email from an allowlisted sender always creates a ticket for a human agent (unless other authentication or suspension checks prevent it).
  • Emails identified as potentially risky or spammy aren't handled by AI agents.

Configure spam and junk email filtering

Admins can configure the spam and junk email filtering options on the Email page in Admin Center.

To configure spam and junk email filtering

  1. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Talk and email > Email.
  2. In the 'Spam and junk email filtering' section at the bottom of the page, select an option for each spam category: Default, Accept, or Suspend.
  3. Click Save.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I configure spam and junk email filtering in Admin Center?

Go to Admin Center > Channels > Talk and email > Email. In the Spam and junk email filtering section at the bottom of the page, choose Default, Accept, or Suspend for each category, then click Save.

What are my options for handling emails in each spam category?

Choose Default to use Zendesk’s default filtering behavior, Accept to create a ticket, or Suspend to send the email to the suspended tickets queue. Categories include phishing, scam or fraud, strong or weak spam signals, marketing and bulk email, low reputation senders, and adult content.

What happens if my email matches more than one spam category?

Zendesk applies the strictest outcome. If any matching category is set to Suspend, Zendesk suspends the email.

Why might my incoming email be flagged as spam or junk?

Zendesk assesses signals related to the message, sender, and email delivery or authentication setup. It does not publish the specific algorithms or exact rules, and no single characteristic necessarily means an email will be flagged. A message may be placed in Suspended tickets for review.

Which email protections apply regardless of my spam filtering settings?

Email containing malware or viruses is always suspended. Email from an allowlisted sender creates a ticket for a human agent unless other authentication or suspension checks prevent it. Emails identified as potentially risky or spammy are not handled by AI agents.

articles.title: Service Incident - November 3, 2026 - AI Agents | AI agents are unresponsive
articles.body:
Summary

On November 3, 2026 from 10:20 to 15:30 UTC AI Agents customers across all pods experienced AI Agents failures, including fallback answers, generic technical reply errors, failed handoffs to human agents, failing actions, and dashboard pages failing to load.

Timeline

November 3, 2026 10:20 UTC | November 3, 2026 02:20 PST

We began receiving alerts from multiple pods, followed by customer tickets reporting issues accessing AI Agents dashboards and end-user messages sent as technical errors.

November 3, 2026 10:58 UTC | November 3, 2026 02:58 PST
We’re investigating an issue affecting AI Agents. Customers may receive fallback responses instead of answers, be unable to escalate conversations to a human agent, or have trouble loading the AI Agents dashboard. Our engineering team is working to identify the cause. We don’t yet have an estimated recovery time, but we’ll share updates as more information becomes available.

November 3, 2026 11:46 UTC | November 3, 2026 03:46 PST
We’re continuing our recovery efforts for the AI Agents issue. A staged redeployment is in progress, and we’re monitoring its impact across affected services. While this work is underway, some customers may continue to experience the issue. We’re also investigating cases where the problem persists and validating the service before confirming recovery. At this time, we can’t confirm that service has fully recovered or provide an estimated resolution time. We’ll continue to share updates as we learn more.

November 3, 2026 13:05 UTC | November 3, 2026 05:05 PST
We’re seeing signs of improvement following service restarts, but some customers may still have issues with AI Agents responding, handing conversations off to a human agent, or loading the dashboard. Our engineering team is restarting additional affected services and investigating the remaining errors. We apologize for the continued disruption and will share another update as recovery progresses.

November 3, 2026 15:46 UTC |  November 3, 2026 05:46 PST
We’ve identified an additional change needed to restore AI Agents. Our engineering team is working on the change and testing the service. We’re sorry for the continued disruption. We’ll share another update as soon as we have more information.

November 3, 2026 16:20 UTC | November 3, 2026 PST
Our team's recent changes are showing promising improvement in the issue affecting AI Agents services. EU customers may see this improvement already, and we are moving to roll out to US customers momentarily to mitigate impact. Thank you for your continued patience as we work to address the issues seen today.

November 3, 2026 16:53 UTC | November 3, 2026 06:53 PST
We are seeing improvement for most customers affected by the AI Agents issues, but there are some lingering symptoms as the fix finishes rolling out and system function is restored. Our team is monitoring to ensure that all functionality has improved, and we will provide further updates as we approach full recovery.

November 3, 2026 17:42 UTC | November 3, 2026 07:42 PST
We are happy to report that the issues affecting AI Agents have been resolved, and bot conversations and other affected functionality should be restored at this time. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

Root Cause Analysis

During an unscheduled secret rotation, the updated secret did not propagate to all services correctly. This caused AI Agent services to be unable to sign and validate tokens for service-to-service communication and led to disrupted agent workflows: AI Agents entered fallback behavior, and instead sent technical error replies, and could not escalate. Additionally as a result of this communication failure, AI Agent dashboards also became stuck in a refresh loop and could not be loaded.

Resolution

We corrected the issue by redeploying and applying the missing secrets across all impacted services. Once this was complete, error rates and product behavior returned to normal across products and features in all pods by 15:15 UTC. Due to the nature of our infrastructure partitioning some customers may have experienced earlier recovery.

We performed an audit of our outcome based pricing engine during the incident and we can confirm there were no observed miscounting of resolutions during the incident. If you have further questions on usage billing during this incident please reach out to your Zendesk representative.

Remediation Items

  1. Review and reinforce deployment and monitoring standards: including unscheduled secret rotations.
  2. Production and pre-production monitor review: to identify and implement improvements to proactively identify similar token propagation failures.
  3. Review and update playbook for AI agents workarounds: to effectively communicate verified mitigation steps we can recommend during similar incidents.
  4. Analyze outcome based pricing engine for any billing inaccuracies: We observed no inaccurate usage charges during our review of this incident.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Error: AADSTS650056 appears when signing in to Zendesk
articles.title: Error: AADSTS650056 appears when signing in to Zendesk
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When I try to sign in to Zendesk using single sign-on (SSO) with Microsoft Entra, I see the error:

AADSTS650056: Misconfigured application. This could be due to one of the following: the client has not listed any permissions for 'AAD Graph' in the requested permissions in the client's application registration. Or, the admin has not consented in the tenant. Or, check the application identifier in the request to ensure it matches the configured client application identifier. Or, check the certificate in the request to ensure it's valid. Please contact your admin to fix the configuration or consent on behalf of the tenant. Client app ID: xxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxx.

Root cause

Microsoft Entra ID, not Zendesk, returns the error AADSTS650056: Misconfigured application before the user authenticates. It usually means the Issuer in the Zendesk SAML request doesn't match the Identifier (Entity ID) configured in the Entra enterprise application.

Zendesk sends the Issuer as <subdomain>.zendesk.com, so the Entra value must use a format Entra accepts.

Resolution steps

The most common mistake is the https:// prefix. In most cases, https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com fails where <subdomain>.zendesk.com works. If the error occurs, test both formats in the Entra Identifier (Entity ID) field, with and without https://, and save after each change.

For more information, see Error AADSTS650056: Misconfigured application.

articles.name: When can I reshare a ticket after unsharing?
articles.title: When can I reshare a ticket after unsharing?
articles.body:
Question

I have a ticket shared with another Zendesk account. I want to unshare the ticket and then share it again. How long do I need to wait before resharing?

Answer

Wait at least 1 to 2 minutes after unsharing a ticket before you share it again. This makes sure the ticket appears in the partner account right away.

You don't have to wait. But if you reshare too soon, one of the following can happen:

  • Within the first few seconds of unsharing: the unshare may not have finished processing on the partner account's side. The share may not reach the partner account correctly, and the ticket may not appear.
  • Within about 60 seconds of unsharing: the ticket may take several minutes to appear in the partner account.

For more information, see Sharing and unsharing tickets.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-11-06
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-11-06
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of last month's releases.

This week's release notes include:

  • Knowledge
  • AI Agents
  • AI/Copilot
  • App Marketplace
  • Products with no updates this week

Knowledge

New

  • Knowledge Graph
    • Connectors are now available for Gong, Shopify, Dynamics 365, Zammad, and Linear.
    • Suggested actions in the Knowledge panel now remain available for the rest of your session. You can refresh them, expand or collapse them, and they respect your viewing history for linked articles and posts.
    • The Universal Connector setup now displays a banner if AI mapping doesn't suggest any data mappings. The connection form also checks that you've selected an authentication method before you continue.

Fixed

  • Knowledge
    • Content from Contentful no longer intermittently disappears from Help Center search results.
    • The Contentful connector no longer syncs draft content types.
    • Jira connections no longer show a misleading syncing status.
    • Quick answers in the Knowledge sidebar app now appear in the user's language instead of English.
    • Articles opened from citations now display correctly in the Knowledge panel.
    • You can no longer enable more than five suggested questions for a locale. The suggested questions page is also more accessible with a keyboard and screen readers.
  • Procedures
    • Procedure version history now shows unpublished events.
  • Article Editor
    • Inserting a callout no longer disrupts list items or numbering.
    • The correct empty state now appears when suggested changes can't be anchored.
    • Archiving an article in recommendation mode now takes you to the archived view.
    • Selecting Update article for a recommendation on a secondary brand now opens the correct brand.
    • API articles are no longer incorrectly marked as legacy.
    • Accepting an AI translation now republishes an already-published translation when needed.
  • Help Center
    • The updated Copenhagen theme now loads locale-specific translations before falling back to the base language. Install v4.53.6 to get the fix.
    • Help Center search and community posts now have improved heading structure, image alternative text, and link distinction for people using screen readers or a keyboard.

AI Agents

New

  • AI Agents Insights
    • The AI agent launchpad is a guided experience that speeds up setup, helps you get value sooner, and supports performance improvements across AI agents. The rollout starts November 5 and ends November 30. See Using the agent overview to monitor and manage a specific AI agent.

AI/Copilot

New

  • Create custom summaries for tickets and calls
  • You can now specify brands, groups, and ticket tags to control when auto assist considers each procedure. See  Creating procedures for auto assist.
  • Auto assist now filters internal notes before using them. This lets it use private team context to help resolve tickets without exposing sensitive information to end users.
  • AI Translations
    • The AI translations glossary is generally available to all customers with the Copilot add-on, giving you control over how AI-generated translations handle your business-specific terminology.
    • Messaging translations are now saved: Translated agent replies in messaging channels are saved and shown again in Agent Workspace. Agents don't have to wait for a conversation to be translated again when they return to it. Another agent can also view and translate the conversation.

Fixed

  • Auto assist no longer regenerates plans unnecessarily when internal triggers update. It also now parses media without captions and file attachments into ticket context, helping prevent it from over- or underreacting.
  • Auto assist now retains customer details, such as names and email addresses, submitted through bot forms. Agents don't have to ask customers to repeat information they've already provided.
  • Auto assist no longer removes key customer details from forwarded emails in a ticket's opening message.
  • Auto assist now copies procedure IDs correctly, preventing incorrect suggestions.
  • You can now use View related tickets for IT trigger recommendations to see the tickets associated with each recommendation.
  • Accepted topic suggestions now appear in the topic list even when their categories or subcategories are under review, and tickets are classified with those topics.

articles.name: Performing A/B testing on generative procedures
articles.title: Performing A/B testing on generative procedures
articles.body:
A/B testing allows you to compare a livegenerative procedurewith an updated draft version of the same procedure using real customer conversations. It compares their automated resolution rate to determine whether the draft version performs better than the live version. This helps you decide whether to publish your updated procedure or keep the existing version.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Use A/B testing to compare a live generative procedure with one draft variant in real customer conversations and see whether the draft improves automated resolution rates. Admins can set traffic splits and test duration, review results and conversation metrics, and publish a winning variant. Tests can be canceled at any time; outcomes are a variant win or inconclusive.

A/B testing allows you to compare a live generative procedure with an updated draft version of the same procedure using real customer conversations. It compares their automated resolution rate to determine whether the draft version performs better than the live version. This helps you decide whether to publish your updated procedure or keep the existing version.

You must be an admin to use A/B testing.

This article contains the following topics:

  • About A/B testing
  • Creating an A/B test
  • Canceling an ongoing A/B test
  • Viewing A/B test results

About A/B testing

A/B testing compares two versions of a generative procedure to determine which performs better:

  • Control: The live procedure currently used by your AI agent.
  • Variant: A draft version of the same procedure that contains changes you want to test against the control.

The test uses real customer conversations to compare the automated resolution rates of the live procedure (control) and draft version (variant) to determine whether the variant performs better at resolving customer requests without intervention from a human agent.

Limitations of A/B testing

A/B testing currently has the following limitations:

  • Automated resolution rate is the only evaluation metric: You can evaluate test performance based on the automated resolution rate only.
  • One-sided testing: The test determines only whether the variant outperforms the control. Possible outcomes indicate whether the variant wins, or the result is inconclusive. It cannot declare the control as the winner.
  • One variant per test: You can test only one draft procedure against the live procedure at a time.

Creating an A/B test

Admins can create an A/B test in the AI agents workspace.

To create an A/B test

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar, then select A/B tests.
  3. In the top-right corner, click + New A/B test.
  4. Enter a Name and Description of your test.

  5. Select a procedure from the list to use as the Control.
  6. Select a version of the same procedure to use as the Variant.
  7. (Optional) Next to the control and variant, update the percent of customer conversations that should be directed to each procedure version. By default, the traffic split is set to 50/50, but you can assign more traffic to the control for a more conservative test.
  8. Select either of the following durations:
    • Conversation count: The test runs for up to 375 conversations.
    • Fixed duration: Set a start date and end date for the test.
  9. Click Start A/B test to begin testing.

Canceling an ongoing A/B test

You can cancel an A/B test at any time before it reaches its configured end condition.

To cancel an A/B test

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar, then select A/B tests.
  3. In the top-right, click the options menu and select End experiment.

Once you cancel an A/B test, the test ends immediately, and no winner is declared. But you can still access the canceled test and view the metrics collected before cancellation for reference.

Viewing A/B test results

While an A/B test is ongoing and after it’s complete, you can view its results to compare the performance of the control and variant.

To view A/B test results

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar, then select A/B tests.
  3. Select the ongoing or completed A/B test you want to review.

The dashboard displays the following metrics:

  • Traffic split: A pie chart showing the total number of conversations that use the control or the variant.
  • BSAT score: The percentage of customers who rate the AI agent 4 or 5 after their conversation. It is calculated by dividing the number of ratings of 4 or 5 by the total number of ratings received, and multiplying by 100.
  • Automated resolutions rate: The percentage of eligible conversations that end with a verified resolution.
  • Automated resolutions (AR) over time: A time-series view of the AR over the duration of the experiment.
  • Assisted escalations rate: The percentage of eligible conversations in which the AI agent helped the customer before handing the conversation to a human agent.
  • Assisted escalations over time: A time-series view of the assisted escalation rate over the duration of the experiment.

Understanding A/B test outcomes

A completed A/B test can have one of the following outcomes:

  • Variant wins: The draft version achieved a statistically significantly higher automated resolution rate than the live version. You can optionally publish the winning variant by clicking View and publish from the test results.
  • Inconclusive: The test could not confirm that the draft version performs better than the live procedure because the difference in automated resolution rates was not statistically significant.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I create an A/B test for a generative procedure?

You must be an admin. In the AI agents workspace, select an AI agent, go to Test > A/B tests, and click + New A/B test. Name and describe the test, choose the live procedure as the control and a draft version of that same procedure as the variant, set the test duration, and click Start A/B test.

What traffic split and duration can I choose for my A/B test?

The default traffic split is 50/50, and you can adjust the percentages to send more conversations to the control for a more conservative test. You can run the test for a specified conversation count, for which a recommended count is provided based on the split and control’s automated resolution rate, or set a fixed start and end date.

What are the limitations of my A/B test?

Automated resolution rate is the only metric used to evaluate performance. A test can compare only one draft variant with the live control, and it can determine whether the variant wins or the result is inconclusive; it cannot declare the control the winner.

How do I cancel an ongoing A/B test, and what happens afterward?

In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent, go to Test > A/B tests, open the options menu, and select End experiment. The test ends immediately with no winner declared. You can still access it and review metrics collected before cancellation.

How can I review my A/B test results and determine whether I can publish the variant?

In Test > A/B tests, select an ongoing or completed test. The dashboard shows the traffic split, BSAT score, automated resolution rate and its trend, and assisted escalation rate and its trend. You can click View conversations to inspect included conversations. A completed test reports either Variant wins—meaning the variant’s automated resolution rate was statistically significantly higher—or Inconclusive. If the variant wins, you can optionally publish it with View and publish.

articles.name: How can I keep specific use cases on repeated questions in AI agents?
articles.title: How can I keep specific use cases on repeated questions in AI agents?
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I want repeated questions on a specific topic, such as legal or compliance, to enter the same strict, dialogue-driven use case every time. After the use case completes, an immediate follow-up on the same topic goes to clarification, a knowledge search, or a generative reply instead of re-entering the use case.

Root cause

This is intended behavior designed to prevent conversation loops. An AI agent can't select the same use case twice in a row, so the system doesn't guarantee immediate re-entry into a use case. In addition, there's a limit on how many times a conversation can loop through the same block in a dialogue. If the flow passes through the same block three times (for example, if you've linked back to earlier blocks), the AI agent stops attempting to generate a response.

  • After a use case finishes, the AI agent routes a follow-up that would map to the same use case elsewhere, such as a clarification or knowledge search. After another step has run, the agent can select the use case again.
  • The restriction applies to the selection of a use case. If you link from one dialogue to a use case, no selection takes place. The agent still treats the original use case as the last one selected. Linking back to a use case or to the welcome reply is therefore not a reliable way around the restriction.

Resolution steps

No setting guarantees that an AI agent can enter a use case twice in a row. As a workaround, end the use case by linking back to the welcome reply, and have the welcome reply route to the use case through intent detection.

To set up this workaround:

  1. Open the AI agent and edit the use case that must repeat
  2. At the end of its dialogue, add a step that links to the Welcome reply
  3. In the welcome reply, add a Customer message block with an Intent predicted branch for that topic and link it to the use case
  4. Publish your changes and test with consecutive questions on the topic, for example, two order update questions back-to-back, to confirm the use case runs each time

For more information, see Customizing the welcome reply in AI agent conversations.

Notes

  • Zendesk doesn't guarantee this behavior. Test it in your own environment, and re-test after you change your flows.
  • This workaround works around the loop-prevention restriction, which you can't turn off. The agent doesn't select the same use case twice in a row. Because a link isn't a selection, the agent can still treat the original use case as the last one selected. That is why the intent-detection branches matter, and why linking to the welcome reply with no branches may be inconsistent.

articles.name: Adding objects as the input or output of custom actions
articles.title: Adding objects as the input or output of custom actions
articles.body:
Custom actions can send and receive different types of data when they run in action flows, including JSON object data. You can add an object or an array of objects as the input of a custom action, then map that input to an API request. You can also save an object from an API response as an output to use in later action flow steps.

What's my plan?
All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

You can add JSON objects or arrays of objects as inputs to custom actions, map them to API requests, and save objects from API responses as outputs for later action flow steps. Use structured inputs for data such as customer profiles, orders, or line items, and pass returned data between actions without rebuilding its properties.

Custom actions can send and receive different types of data when they run in action flows, including JSON object data. You can add an object or an array of objects as the input of a custom action, then map that input to an API request. You can also save an object from an API response as an output to use in later action flow steps.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Understanding objects in custom actions
  • Adding objects as the input of custom actions
  • Adding objects as the output of custom actions

Related article:

  • Creating custom actions for auto assist, AI agents, and action flows

Understanding objects in custom actions

An object is a group of related values organized as key-value pairs using the JSON format. For example, an order object can include an order ID, customer email address, shipping address, and line items. An array of objects is a list of objects, such as the line items in an order.

Example object:

{
  "customer_id": "12345",
  "shipping_address": {
    "city": "Melbourne",
    "country": "Australia"
  }
}

Example array of objects:

[
  {
    "product_id": "A-100",
    "quantity": 2
  },
  {
    "product_id": "B-200",
    "quantity": 1
  }
]

In an action flow, you can map an object output from an earlier step to the input of another custom action. When the flow runs, the complete object is sent to the custom action.

Adding objects as the input of custom actions

Add an object input to a custom action if the action makes an API request that requires a structured value, such as an order, customer profile, or ticket. Add an array-of-objects input when an API request requires a list of structured items, such as order line items, assets, or organization memberships.

To add an object or array-of-objects input to a custom action

  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Custom actions.

  2. Create a custom action or open the custom action you want to edit.

  3. In the Inputs section, click Add input.

  4. Enter a clear Name and Description for the input.

    Use a singular name for an object, such as order, customer, or shipping_address. Use a plural name for an array of objects, such as line_items, assets, or memberships.

  5. For Type, select Object or Array of objects depending on the data that the API expects, then click Next.

  6. Paste a representative JSON object or JSON schema that describes the object the API endpoint expects.

    When you add an object input, define its structure using either of the following:

    • A representative JSON example from the API documentation or a successful API response
    • A JSON schema that describes the required object structure

    Click Next when you're done.

  7. On the next screen, review the object properties.

    Select which properties are required for this action. By default all properties are selected, but you can deselect the ones you won't need.

  8. Click Add input.

  9. In API configuration, add the input to the request body, query parameters, or headers as required by the external API.

    To add the input to the request body, click {+} and select the object input. Do not manually recreate the object properties unless the API requires individual values.

  10. Complete the remaining custom action configuration, then click Save.

Adding objects as the output of custom actions

Add an object output when you want to make an object returned from an API request available to later steps in an action flow. For example, you might retrieve a customer profile, then pass that profile to another custom action that updates the customer in an external system.

To add an object output to a custom action

  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Custom actions.
  2. Create a custom action or open the custom action you want to edit.
  3. In the Outputs section, click Add output.
  4. Enter test data to send to your external service to return a representative response, then click Make API call.

    This information is sent to your external service, which returns a representative JSON response. You can proceed if the test is successful.

  5. Click Add next to the object you want to save as a variable.

    The object is the data that you want to pass to later steps in your flow.

  6. Enter a Name andDescription for the variable, then click Next.
  7. If a property is missing from your object, add it to the editable JSON schema, then click Next.
  8. If you're satisfied with the property list, click Add output, then click Done.
  9. Click Save to save the custom action.

Article Q&A

Click to view

What’s the difference between an object and an array of objects in a custom action?

An object is a group of related key-value pairs in JSON, such as a customer profile. An array of objects is a list of objects, such as order line items. In an action flow, you can map an object output from an earlier step to another custom action’s input; the complete object is sent when the flow runs.

How do I add an object or array of objects as a custom action input?

In Admin Center, go to Apps and integrations > Actions > Custom actions, create or edit an action, and select Add input. Enter a name and description, choose Object or Array of objects based on what the API expects, and provide a representative JSON example or JSON schema. Review the properties, choose which are required, and add the input.

How do I send my object input in the API request?

In API configuration, add the input to the request body, query parameters, or headers as required by the external API. For the request body, click {+} and select the object input. Don’t manually recreate its properties unless the API requires individual values.

How do I save an API response object for a later action flow step?

In the custom action’s Outputs section, enter test data and click Make API call to get a representative JSON response. Click Add next to the object you want to save, name and describe the variable, and add any missing properties to the editable JSON schema. Then click Add output, Done, and Save.

articles.name: Service Incident - October 29, 2026 - Support/Knowledge | All Pods - Zendesk down with CDN error related to regional connectivity issue in Mexico
articles.title: Service Incident - October 29, 2026 - Support/Knowledge | All Pods - Zendesk down with CDN error related to regional connectivity issue in Mexico
articles.body:
Summary

Between 23:25 UTC on 28 October 2026 and 00:35 UTC on 29 October 2026, some users connecting from Mexico were unable to access or sign in to Zendesk Support. Users may have seen an error page or experienced a connection timeout while trying to connect.

Timeline

October 29, 2026 00:28 UTC | October 28, 2026 05:28 PM PT

We are aware that some customers are encountering error messages from our CDN partner when accessing Zendesk Support. Our team is actively investigating this issue as a priority. We apologize for the disruption and will share further updates as more information becomes available.

October 29, 2026 00:54 UTC | October 28, 2026 05:54 PM PT

Our engineers have identified a network connectivity issue affecting customers in the Mexico region, and we are now seeing signs of recovery. Please try accessing Zendesk Support again and let us know whether access has returned to normal or if you continue to experience issues. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

October 29, 2026 01:26 UTC | October 28, 2026 06:26 PM PT

Our CDN partner has identified a regional outage affecting customers in Mexico and is working to resolve it. We continue to observe improvement and recovery in access to Zendesk Support. We are monitoring the situation and will share further updates as they become available. Thank you for your patience.

October 29, 2026 07:48 UTC | October 28, 2026 06:26 PM PT

Following our CDN partner’s rerouting of traffic, we have closely monitored the service and confirmed recovery for customers in the Mexico region. Access to Zendesk Support has returned to normal. Thank you for your patience during this disruption.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a network issue at one of our service provider locations in Mexico. Some requests could not be completed or took too long to connect until traffic was redirected through other available locations.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, our content delivery provider redirected traffic away from the affected location in Querétaro, Mexico, to other available locations. This restored normal connectivity and access to Zendesk Support.

Remediation Items

  1. Improve early detection: Review and enhance monitoring so network access issues are identified, assessed, and escalated as quickly as possible.
  2. Route incidents to the right team: Confirm that issues involving external providers are automatically directed to the appropriate response team, reducing delays in investigation and recovery.
  3. Strengthen response procedures: Review and update the documented response process for network access incidents, including clear ownership, investigation steps, and recovery guidance.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.
